ai.description: Duttaphrynus chandai is a small toad reaching 35–40 mm. It is dark brown with irregular black spots and possesses a distinct, thickened parotoid gland and a prominent, continuous cranial crest.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus chandai* is best distinguished by its unique, prominent, and continuous glandular ridge extending from the snout tip to the parotoid glands.
ai.habitat: *Duttaphrynus chandai* inhabits high-altitude montane forests and rocky stream beds in Nagaland, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nagaland Montane Torrent Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus chandai* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in strings within montane streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Duttaphrynus chandai* is endemic to the high-altitude montane forests of Nagaland in Northeast India, typically occurring at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nagaland Montane Torrent Toad emits a series of high-pitched, pulsed trills while perched on mossy rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
